detail.body:
## Motivation

Gemma-3 multimodal uses **bidirectional attention among image tokens** during prefill (text stays causal). In SGLang this is realized by `Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration.prepare_attn_masks()` building a dense per-sequence mask — but that path is gated to `TritonAttnBackend` only (see the note in `gemma3_mm.py`: *"only the TritonAttnBackend supports bidirectional attention; other backends have not yet implemented this"*).

On the Intel XPU attention backend the mask was never applied, so image tokens ran plain **causal** attention, degrading vision-heavy tasks while leaving text unaffected.

On Intel Arc Pro B60 (`--attention-backend intel_xpu`, tp1), `docvqa_val` ANLS:

| backend | ANLS |
|---|---|
| intel_xpu (before) | 59.4 |
| triton (same HW) | 64.1 |
| H200 (ref) | 65.0 |
| **intel_xpu (this PR, sgl-kernel-xpu native)** | **67.46** |

Text-only `gsm8k_cot` is unchanged between intel_xpu and triton, consistent with the gap being image-specific.

## Modifications

This does the bidirectional masking **in the kernel** (via sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495), keeping the sglang path a normal flash-attn call — no attention fallback in the model runner.

- `models/gemma3_mm.py::prepare_attn_masks`: for `XPUAttentionBackend`, build a per-token block id over whole sequences (image index, `-1` for text) and store it on the backend (`is_xpu()`-guarded lazy import; the Triton path is unchanged). None when this extend holds fewer than two tokens of any image.
- `layers/attention/xpu_backend.py::forward_extend`: when present, run non-causal and pass `bidirectional_block_ids` to `flash_attn_with_kvcache`; the kernel re-imposes causal for block-less tokens and keeps same-block (image) tokens bidirectional. With a cached prefix (radix hit or a later chunk), q is padded to whole sequences so the kernel sees a full prefill, and only the extend rows are kept. On sliding-window layers the window is dropped only when it cannot clip a key; longer prompts keep local attention.
- `layers/layernorm.py::forward_xpu`: make the input contiguous before `gemma_rmsnorm` (it requires a contiguous last dim, which a sliced hidden state may not have) so Gemma-3 loads on XPU.
- `test/registered/xpu/test_xpu_gemma3_bidirectional_attn.py`: sliding-window bound and image-after-cached-prefix against a dense reference.

Depends on the companion kernel PR sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495 (`bidirectional_block_ids`).

## Accuracy

`docvqa_val` (lmms-eval, ANLS), Intel Arc Pro B60, tp1, `--enable-multimodal --attention-backend intel_xpu` with default radix cache and chunked prefill: **59.4 → 67.46** over the full 5349-sample val set (67.48 with full prefill and radix off), above the H200 reference (65.0). `gsm8k_cot` (text) unchanged. The kernel is unit-tested against an fp32 reference on the companion PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Lint: ruff / ruff-format / isort clean.
- [x] Bidirectional prefill is prefill-only; decode / CUDA-graph paths are untouched.

+"""Gemma-3 bidirectional image attention on XPU (sgl-kernel-xpu bidirectional_block_ids).
+
+Guards the cases the kernel mask cannot express directly: a sliding-window layer
+whose prompt exceeds the window must keep local attention, and image tokens in an
+extend after a cached prefix must still attend bidirectionally.
+"""
+
+import unittest
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+
+from sglang.test.ci.ci_register import register_xpu_ci
+from sglang.test.test_utils import CustomTestCase
+
+register_xpu_ci(est_time=30, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")
+
+PAGE, H, HKV, D = 128, 8, 4, 128
+
+
+def _paged_inputs(seq_len, dev):
+    q = torch.randn(seq_len, H, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    k = torch.randn(seq_len, HKV, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    v = torch.randn(seq_len, HKV, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    npages = (seq_len + PAGE - 1) // PAGE
+    k_cache = torch.zeros(npages * PAGE, HKV, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+    v_cache = torch.zeros_like(k_cache)
+    k_cache[:seq_len], v_cache[:seq_len] = k, v
+    return (
+        q,
+        k,
+        v,
+        k_cache.view(npages, PAGE, HKV, D),
+        v_cache.view(npages, PAGE, HKV, D),
+    )
+
+
+def _reference(q, k, v, allow, scale):
+    k = k.float().repeat_interleave(H // HKV, dim=1)
+    v = v.float().repeat_interleave(H // HKV, dim=1)
+    scores = torch.einsum("qhd,khd->hqk", q.float(), k) * scale
+    scores = scores.masked_fill(~allow.unsqueeze(0), float("-inf"))
+    return torch.einsum("hqk,khd->qhd", scores.softmax(dim=-1), v)
+
+
+def _image_batch(prefix_lens, extend_lens, image_spans):
+    image_items = [
+        SimpleNamespace(mm_items=[SimpleNamespace(is_image=lambda: True, offsets=s)])
+        for s in image_spans
+    ]
+    return SimpleNamespace(
+        batch_size=len(prefix_lens),
+        extend_prefix_lens_cpu=prefix_lens,
+        extend_seq_lens_cpu=extend_lens,
+        mm_inputs=image_items,
+    )
+
+
+def _build_block_ids(forward_batch, device):
+    from sglang.srt.models.gemma3_mm import Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration
+
+    return Gemma3ForConditionalGeneration._build_xpu_image_block_ids(
+        forward_batch=forward_batch, device=device
+    )
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    hasattr(torch, "xpu") and torch.xpu.is_available(), "requires an Intel XPU"
+)
+class TestXPUGemma3SlidingWindowBound(CustomTestCase):
+    WINDOW_LEFT = 63
+    SPAN = (8, 40)
+
+    def _run(self, seq_len):
+        from sgl_kernel.flash_attn import (
+            build_bidirectional_block_ids,
+            flash_attn_with_kvcache,
+        )
+
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.xpu_backend import (
+            _bidirectional_image_attn_args,
+        )
+
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        dev = "xpu"
+        scale = D**-0.5
+        q, k, v, k_cache, v_cache = _paged_inputs(seq_len, dev)
+        block_ids, window_size = _bidirectional_image_attn_args(
+            block_ids=build_bidirectional_block_ids([seq_len], [[self.SPAN]], dev),
+            window_size=(self.WINDOW_LEFT, 0),
+            max_seqlen_k=seq_len,
+        )
+        out = flash_attn_with_kvcache(
+            q=q,
+            k_cache=k_cache,
+            v_cache=v_cache,
+            page_table=torch.arange(
+                k_cache.shape[0], device=dev, dtype=torch.int32
+            ).view(1, -1),
+            cache_seqlens=torch.tensor([seq_len], device=dev, dtype=torch.int32),
+            cu_seqlens_q=torch.tensor([0, seq_len], device=dev, dtype=torch.int32),
+            max_seqlen_q=seq_len,
+            softmax_scale=scale,
+            causal=block_ids is None,
+            window_size=window_size,
+            bidirectional_block_ids=block_ids,
+        )
+        torch.xpu.synchronize()
+        rows = torch.arange(seq_len, device=dev).view(-1, 1)
+        cols = torch.arange(seq_len, device=dev).view(1, -1)
+        return out.float(), q, k, v, rows, cols, scale
+
+    def test_prompt_longer_than_window_keeps_local_attention(self):
+        """Keys beyond the sliding window must stay masked once the prompt outgrows
+        the window, even though the batch carries image block ids."""
+        out, q, k, v, rows, cols, scale = self._run(seq_len=200)
+        local = (cols <= rows) & (rows - cols <= self.WINDOW_LEFT)
+        want = _reference(q, k, v, local, scale)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, want, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+    def test_prompt_within_window_keeps_bidirectional_image(self):
+        """At kv length == left window + 1 the window clips nothing, so the image
+        span must still be attended bidirectionally."""
+        out, q, k, v, rows, cols, scale = self._run(seq_len=self.WINDOW_LEFT + 1)
+        allow = cols <= rows
+        begin, last = self.SPAN
+        allow[begin : last + 1, begin : last + 1] = True
+        want = _reference(q, k, v, allow, scale)
+        torch.testing.assert_close(out, want, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2)
+
+
+@unittest.skipUnless(
+    hasattr(torch, "xpu") and torch.xpu.is_available(), "requires an Intel XPU"
+)
+class TestXPUGemma3ImageAfterCachedPrefix(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_matches_full_bidirectional_attention(self):
+        """With a cached prefix (radix hit or an earlier chunk), image tokens in the
+        extend must attend bidirectionally and see the whole prefix. The batch mixes
+        a page-aligned prefix, an unaligned prefix with an image straddling it, and
+        no prefix with an image cut by the chunk end."""
+        from sglang.srt.layers.attention.xpu_backend import XPUAttentionBackend
+
+        torch.manual_seed(0)
+        dev = "xpu"
+        scale = D**-0.5
+        prefix_lens, extend_lens = [128, 50, 0], [100, 90, 70]
+        image_spans = [[(140, 190)], [(30, 100)], [(40, 90)]]
+        seq_lens = [p + e for p, e in zip(prefix_lens, extend_lens)]
+        pages_per_seq = [(s + PAGE - 1) // PAGE for s in seq_lens]
+        num_pages = sum(pages_per_seq)
+
+        # Hand pages out in reverse so each sequence's pages are non-contiguous.
+        free_pages = list(range(num_pages))[::-1]
+        req_to_token = torch.zeros(len(seq_lens), 256, dtype=torch.int32, device=dev)
+        for i, n in enumerate(pages_per_seq):
+            pages = torch.tensor([free_pages.pop(0) for _ in range(n)], device=dev)
+            slots = (pages[:, None] * PAGE + torch.arange(PAGE, device=dev)).flatten()
+            req_to_token[i, : n * PAGE] = slots.to(torch.int32)
+        k_flat = torch.randn(num_pages * PAGE, HKV, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+        v_flat = torch.randn_like(k_flat)
+        q = torch.randn(sum(extend_lens), H, D, device=dev, dtype=torch.bfloat16)
+
+        backend = XPUAttentionBackend.__new__(XPUAttentionBackend)
+        backend.num_splits = 0
+        to_dev = lambda x: torch.tensor(x, device=dev, dtype=torch.int32)
+        block_ids = _build_block_ids(
+            _image_batch(prefix_lens, extend_lens, image_spans), dev
+        )
+        out = backend._forward_image_blocks_after_prefix(
+            q=q,
+            key_cache=k_flat.view(num_pages, PAGE, HKV, D),
+            value_cache=v_flat.view(num_pages, PAGE, HKV, D),
+            page_table=req_to_token[:, ::PAGE] // PAGE,
+            forward_batch=SimpleNamespace(
+                extend_prefix_lens_cpu=prefix_lens,
+                extend_prefix_lens=to_dev(prefix_lens),
+                extend_seq_lens=to_dev(extend_lens),
+            ),
+            metadata=SimpleNamespace(
+                cache_seqlens_int32=to_dev(seq_lens),
+                cu_seqlens_k=torch.nn.functional.pad(
+                    torch.cumsum(to_dev(seq_lens), dim=0, dtype=torch.int32), (1, 0)
+                ),
+                max_seq_len_k=max(seq_lens),
+            ),
+            block_ids=block_ids,
+            scale=scale,
+            softcap=0.0,
+        )
+        torch.xpu.synchronize()
+
+        q_start = 0
+        for i, (prefix_len, seq_len) in enumerate(zip(prefix_lens, seq_lens)):
+            slots = req_to_token[i, :seq_len].long()
+            rows = torch.arange(prefix_len, seq_len, device=dev).view(-1, 1)
+            cols = torch.arange(seq_len, device=dev).view(1, -1)
+            allow = cols <= rows
+            for begin, last in image_spans[i]:
+                allow |= (
+                    (rows >= begin) & (rows <= last) & (cols >= begin) & (cols <= last)
+                )
+            q_end = q_start + seq_len - prefix_len
+            want = _reference(
+                q[q_start:q_end], k_flat[slots], v_flat[slots], allow, scale
+            )
+            torch.testing.assert_close(
+                out[q_start:q_end].float(), want, rtol=2e-2, atol=2e-2
+            )
+            q_start = q_end
+
+
+class TestXPUGemma3ImageBlockIds(CustomTestCase):
+    def test_image_only_in_cached_prefix_needs_no_mask(self):
+        """A text-only extend after a cached image is exact under causal attention
+        and must take the plain causal path."""
+        self.assertIsNone(
+            _build_block_ids(_image_batch([256], [50], [[(10, 200)]]), "cpu")
+        )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    unittest.main()

+        layer: RadixAttention,
+        key_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        value_cache: torch.Tensor,
+        page_table: torch.Tensor,
+        cache_seqlens: torch.Tensor,
+        cu_seqlens_q: torch.Tensor,
+    ) -> torch.Tensor:
+        # Full per-sequence K/V is read back from the paged cache via
+        # page_table/cache_seqlens, so prefix (radix), page_size>1 and the SWA
+        # pool are handled uniformly. Each mask is [q_len, total_len] with
+        # total_len == cache_seqlens[i]; queries are the last q_len tokens. SWA
+        # layers AND in the (left=window,0) band (no-op when total_len <= window).
+        import torch.nn.functional as F
+
+        h_q = layer.tp_q_head_num
+        h_kv = layer.tp_k_head_num
+        d = layer.head_dim
+        dv = layer.v_head_dim
+        q = q.contiguous().view(-1, h_q, d)
+        key_cache = key_cache.reshape(-1, h_kv, d)
+        value_cache = value_cache.reshape(-1, h_kv, dv)
+
+        cu = cu_seqlens_q.tolist()
+        seqlens = cache_seqlens.tolist()
+        masks = self.mm_bidirectional_masks
+        is_swa = (
+            layer.sliding_window_size is not None and layer.sliding_window_size > -1
+        )
+        rep = h_q // h_kv
+        out = q.new_empty((q.shape[0], h_q, dv))
+
+        for i in range(len(masks)):
+            s, e = cu[i], cu[i + 1]
+            q_len = e - s
+            total_len = int(seqlens[i])
+
+            n_pages = (total_len + self.page_size - 1) // self.page_size
+            slots = page_table[i, :n_pages]
+            kv_slots = (
+                slots
+                if self.page_size == 1
+                else (
+                    slots[:, None] * self.page_size
+                    + torch.arange(self.page_size, device=slots.device)[None, :]
+                ).reshape(-1)
+            )
+            kv_slots = kv_slots[:total_len]
+            kf = key_cache[kv_slots]  # [total_len, h_kv, d]
+            vf = value_cache[kv_slots]  # [total_len, h_kv, dv]
+
+            attn_mask = masks[i].to(torch.bool)  # [q_len, total_len]
+            if is_swa:
+                q_pos = torch.arange(
+                    total_len - q_len, total_len, device=q.device
+                ).unsqueeze(1)
+                k_pos = torch.arange(total_len, device=q.device).unsqueeze(0)
+                attn_mask = attn_mask & (k_pos >= (q_pos - layer.sliding_window_size))
+
+            qi = q[s:e].transpose(0, 1).unsqueeze(0)  # [1, h_q, q_len, d]
+            kf = kf.transpose(0, 1)  # [h_kv, total_len, d]
+            vf = vf.transpose(0, 1)
+            if rep > 1:
+                kf = kf.repeat_interleave(rep, dim=0)
+                vf = vf.repeat_interleave(rep, dim=0)
+            oi = F.scaled_dot_product_attention(
+                qi,
+                kf.unsqueeze(0),
+                vf.unsqueeze(0),
+                attn_mask=attn_mask,
+                scale=layer.scaling,
+            )  # [1, h_q, q_len, dv]
+            out[s:e] = oi.squeeze(0).transpose(0, 1)
+
+        return out.view(-1, h_q * dv)

issue_comments.body:
Updated this PR to the **native sgl-kernel-xpu** approach instead of the earlier torch/SDPA fallback, per the review (@mingfeima @airMeng). The sglang side is now thin, it builds a per extend-token image-block id and passes `mm_block_id` to `flash_attn_with_kvcache`; the bidirectional masking is done in the kernel.

Companion kernel PR: sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495 (adds the `mm_block_id` prefill mask). This PR depends on it.

- `prepare_attn_masks`: for `XPUAttentionBackend`, build the block ids (image index, `-1` for text); Triton path unchanged.
- `forward_extend`: run non-causal + pass `mm_block_id`; the kernel re-imposes causal for text and keeps image tokens bidirectional.
- `layernorm.forward_xpu`: make the input contiguous before `gemma_rmsnorm` (needs a contiguous last dim) so Gemma-3 loads.

Accuracy unchanged from the fallback: `docvqa_val` (full 5349) **59.4 -> 67.5** on Intel Arc Pro B60, above H200 (65.0). Kernel unit test added on the kernel PR.

The `is_xpu()` import guard from the previous round is retained.

Gentle re-review request. The companion kernel PR (sgl-project/sgl-kernel-xpu#495) has now merged, so the `bidirectional_block_ids` prefill mask this PR depends on is in sgl-kernel-xpu main, and the API here matches it. I've also rebased this branch onto current main (mergeable, CI-clean).

I believe the earlier concerns are addressed: the XPUAttentionBackend import is `is_xpu()`-guarded (no silent fallback to causal), and the earlier "torch fallback would be slow" point no longer applies since the masking is now done natively in the kernel rather than a Python SDPA path. Could you take another look when you have a moment? Happy to adjust anything.
